timeline.change: Production starts in Toyota City. The LX 450 is essentially an FZJ80 Land Cruiser with a new grille, side cladding, wheels, a plusher interior and softer suspension.
US sales start in January 1996 at a $47,995 base price, about $7,000 over the Land Cruiser. Over 5,000 sold in the first year. Fully OBD-II compliant.
Final year. Over 9,000 sold, and Canada gets the LX in place of the Land Cruiser.
Production ends. The V8 LX 470 debuts at the Los Angeles show the same month.

identify.intro: An LX 450 is an 80 Series Land Cruiser in a suit, so the real questions are whether it's a genuine LX and what options it left the factory with.

items.head: VIN
items.body: US trucks start JT6HJ88J. NHTSA's vPIC decoder reads the series as FZJ80L with the 1FZ-FE 4.5 I6, built in Toyota City. The 10th character is the model year (T = 1996, V = 1997).

items.head: LX vs Land Cruiser
items.body: From the outside, only the grille, the side body cladding and the wheels differ from an FZJ80. Inside, look for the LX's leather and extra sound insulation.

items.head: Factory lockers
items.body: Electric front and rear lockers were one of only three factory options. Trucks that have them have locker controls on the dash. Test both in low range on a loose surface.

items.head: Center diff lock
items.body: The center diff locks automatically in low range. US trucks from 1993 lost the high-range switch but kept the wiring, so a plug-in CDL switch can add it back.

items.head: Lug nuts
items.body: From 1995 the 80 Series switched from conical to washer-type lug nuts, so make sure the nuts match the wheels on a truck with aftermarket rims.

values.intro: Prices follow the 80 Series Land Cruiser market. Locked, well-documented, unmodified trucks bring the most.
values.note: Based on the 23 most recent Bring a Trailer LX 450 sales (March–October 2026), which ranged from $8,300 to $67,500 with a median of about $26,000.
